newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end higher on Wall Street rally.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end higher on Wall Street rally.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended stronger on Monday, propelled by another surge on Wall Street as investors cast aside U.S. inflation and rate hike fears.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index gained 43.82 points to close at 6150.73. Trading was moderate at 80 million shares worth C$1.6 billion ($1.2 billion).

"The (U.S.) economy is growing at diminishing rates," said RBC Dominion Securities investment adviser Ira Katzin. "The feeling is now that (U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman) Alan Greenspan may not have to increase interest rates on May 20."

Fewer observers expect that Fed members would hike rates after last week's slew of data pointing to low inflation. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 143 points to reach a new high of 7214 points on Monday.

Investors and mutual fund managers built up cash piles as they sat out the six-week downturn in key North American equity markets, Katzin said. "Now, would you believe, they're all rushing through the same door at the same time?" he said.
In Toronto, all but three of the 14 sub-indices rose, led by consumer products, conglomerates and golds. The decliners were banks, base metals and media.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners 483 to 457, while 297 ended flat.
Last week, the 300 Index added almost five percent as inflation and rate hike fears waned.

The biggest story in Toronto was a stock not even traded on Monday. The Toronto Stock Exchange halted trading in Bre-X Minerals Ltd. for the session after its Busang gold find, once touted as the world's largest, was declared a fraud by consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd late on Sunday.
The TSE said Bre-X trading would resume on Tuesday. Shares closed at 3.23 on Friday.

Barrick Gold Corp., the world's third largest gold producer, jumped 0.85 to 32.25 in active trading. Bullion prices ticked upward on Monday, since -- with the Bre-X gold find worthless -- there was no longer the prospect of millions of ounces being added to world reserves.
Small gold miners dropped as investors debated their value. Indochina Goldfields Ltd. fell 2.30 to 10.70.
